sentences.zh: 女子之行，於親也孝，婦也節，母也義而慈，止矣。

translations.literal: In a woman's conduct, toward parents there is filial piety; as a wife there is chastity; as a mother there is righteousness and kindness — and that is all.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's duty is filial piety to her parents, constancy as a wife, and righteous kindness as a mother—and that is the whole of it.

sentences.zh: 中古以前，書所載後、妃、夫人事，天下化之。

translations.literal: Before the middle antiquity, what books record of empresses, consorts, and wives — the realm was transformed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Before the middle antiquity, the empire was transformed by the empresses, consorts, and wives whose deeds books preserve.

sentences.zh: 後彤史職廢，婦訓、姆則不及於家，故賢女可紀者千載間寥寥相望。

translations.literal: Later the office of the red historian was abandoned; women's instruction and governess rules no longer reached the household, so worthy women worth recording were few and far between across a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Later the office of the red historian was abandoned. Women's instruction and governess rules no longer reached the household, so worthy women worth recording were few and far between across a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 唐興，風化陶淬且數百年，而聞家令姓窈窕淑女，至臨大難，守禮節，白刃不能移，與哲人烈士爭不朽名，寒如霜雪，亦可貴矣。

translations.literal: When Tang rose, customs were refined and tempered for several hundred years; yet one heard of gentlewomen of eminent houses who, facing great calamity, upheld ritual propriety — white blades could not move them — and vied with wise men and martyrs for an undying name, cold as frost and snow: that too is precious.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang rose, customs were refined and tempered for several hundred years; yet one heard of gentlewomen of eminent houses who, facing great calamity, upheld ritual propriety — naked blades could not sway them — and vied with wise men and martyrs for an undying name, cold as frost and snow: that too is precious.

sentences.zh: 今采獲尤顯行者著之篇，以緒正父父、子子、夫夫、婦婦之懿云。

translations.literal: Now I gather those especially manifest and set them forth in this chapter, to continue the excellence of fathers as fathers, sons as sons, husbands as husbands, and wives as wives.
translations.idiomatic: Here I collect women whose virtue shone brightest and set them down in this chapter, to carry forward the excellence of fatherhood, sonship, husbandhood, and wifehood.

sentences.zh: 李德武妻裴，字淑英，安邑公矩之女，以孝聞鄉黨。

translations.literal: Pei, wife of Li Dewu, courtesy name Shuying, daughter of Duke Anyi Pei Ju, was famed for filial piety in her village.
translations.idiomatic: Pei, wife of Li Dewu, courtesy name Shuying, daughter of Duke Anyi Pei Ju, won renown for filial piety in her village.

sentences.zh: 德武在隋，坐事徙嶺南，時嫁方逾歲，矩表離婚。

translations.literal: Dewu in Sui was punished and exiled to Lingnan; when she had been married little more than a year, Ju memorialized for divorce.
translations.idiomatic: Dewu in Sui was punished and exiled to Lingnan; when she had been married little more than a year, Ju submitted a memorial requesting divorce.

sentences.zh: 德武謂裴曰：「我方貶，無還理，君必儷它族，於此長決矣。」

translations.literal: Dewu said to Pei: "I am now demoted with no prospect of return; you must surely marry another clan — here we part for good."
translations.idiomatic: Dewu said to Pei: "I am now demoted with no prospect of return. You must surely marry another clan — here we part for good."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「夫，天也，可背乎？

translations.literal: She answered: "A husband is Heaven — can one turn against Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: She replied: "A husband is Heaven — can one turn against Heaven?

sentences.zh: 願死無它。」

translations.literal: I wish only to die and nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: She asked only to die and for nothing more."

sentences.zh: 欲割耳誓，保姆持不許。

translations.literal: She wished to cut off her ear in oath; the nursemaid held her and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: She wished to cut off her ear in oath. The nursemaid held her and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 夫姻胃，歲時塑望裴致禮惟謹。

translations.literal: Among affinal kin, at seasonal sacrifices Pei sent gifts with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: Among her husband's kin, at seasonal sacrifices Pei sent gifts with utmost care.

sentences.zh: 居不禦薰澤。

translations.literal: At home she did not use perfume or cosmetics.
translations.idiomatic: In her chambers she wore no perfume and used no cosmetics.

sentences.zh: 讀《列女傳》，見述不更嫁者，謂人曰：「不踐二廷，婦人之常，何異而載之書？」

translations.literal: Reading the Biographies of Exemplary Women, she saw those who would not remarry and said to others: "Not serving two courts is a woman's constant — why treat it as extraordinary enough to put in a book?"
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Biographies of Exemplary Women, she saw those who refused to remarry and told others: "Not serving two courts is a woman's constant — why treat it as extraordinary enough to put in a book?"

sentences.zh: 後十年，德武未還，矩決嫁之，斷發不食，矩知不能奪，聽之。

translations.literal: After ten years Dewu had not returned; Ju decided to marry her off; she cut her hair and refused food; Ju knew he could not compel her and yielded.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years Dewu had not returned. Ju decided to marry her off. She cut her hair and refused food. Ju knew he could not compel her and yielded.

sentences.zh: 德武更娶汆朱氏，遇赦還，中道聞其完節，乃遣後妻，為夫婦如初。

translations.literal: Dewu took another wife, the Zhu clan of Quan; encountering amnesty he returned; midway he heard of her intact chastity, sent away the later wife, and husband and wife were as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Dewu took another wife, the Zhu clan of Quan. Encountering amnesty he returned. Midway he heard of her intact chastity, sent away the later wife, and husband and wife were as at first.

sentences.zh: 楊慶妻王者，世充足之女。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Yang Qing, was daughter of the Shizu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing's wife Wang was a daughter of the Shizu clan.

sentences.zh: 慶以河間王子為郇王，守滎陽，陷於世充，故世充妻之，用為管州刺史。

translations.literal: Qing, as son of the Prince of Hejian, was made Prince of Ye, holding Yingyang, and fell to Wang Shichong; therefore Shichong gave him a wife and used him as prefect of Guanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, as son of the Prince of Hejian, was made Prince of Ye, holding Yingyang, and fell to Wang Shichong. Therefore Shichong gave him a wife and used him as prefect of Guanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗攻洛陽，慶謀與王歸唐，謝曰：「鄭以我奉箕帚者，綴公之心，今負恩背義，自為身謀，可若何？

translations.literal: Taizong attacked Luoyang; Qing plotted with Wang to return to Tang; she declined: "Zheng took me to tend the broom and dust — to steady your heart; now to betray favor and turn faithless, scheming for oneself — how can that be?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong attacked Luoyang; Qing plotted with Wang to return to Tang; she declined: "Zheng took me to tend the broom and dust — to steady your heart; now to betray favor and turn faithless, scheming for oneself — how can that be?

sentences.zh: 至長安，則公家婢耳，願送我還東都。」

translations.literal: At Chang'an I would be but your household's serving woman — I beg you send me back to the eastern capital."
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an I would be no more than a serving woman in your household—I beg you to send me back to the eastern capital."

sentences.zh: 慶不聽，王謂左右曰：「唐勝則鄭滅，鄭安則吾夫死，若是，生何益？」

translations.literal: Qing would not listen; Wang said to those about her: "If Tang wins, Zheng is destroyed; if Zheng is secure, my husband dies — in such a case, what good is life?"
translations.idiomatic: Qing would not listen. Wang said to those about her: "If Tang wins, Zheng is destroyed. If Zheng is secure, my husband dies — in such a case, what good is life?"

sentences.zh: 乃飲藥死。

translations.literal: She then took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: She thereupon took poison and perished.

sentences.zh: 慶入朝，官宜州刺史。

translations.literal: Qing entered court and was appointed prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qing entered court and received appointment as prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡妻盧，失其世。

translations.literal: Lu, wife of Fang Xuanling — her lineage is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, wife of Fang Xuanling—the record of her lineage has been lost.

sentences.zh: 玄齡微時，病且死，諉曰：「吾病革，君年少，不可寡居，善事後人。」

translations.literal: When Xuanling was still obscure, he fell gravely ill and urged her: "My illness is desperate; you are young — you must not remain a widow; treat well whoever comes after."
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanling was still obscure, he fell gravely ill and urged her: "My illness is desperate. You are young — you must not remain a widow. Treat well whoever comes after.

sentences.zh: 盧泣入帳中，剔一目示玄齡，明無它。

translations.literal: Lu wept, entered the tent, gouged out one eye to show Xuanling, making clear there was no other.
translations.idiomatic: Lu wept, went into the tent, gouged out one eye to show Xuanling, making plain that her heart was set on no other man.

sentences.zh: 會玄齡良愈，禮之終身。

translations.literal: Xuanling then recovered fully and honored her to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling then made a full recovery and honored her for the rest of his days.

sentences.zh: 王蘭英者，獨狐師仁之姆。

translations.literal: Wang Lanying was nurse-mother to Dugu Shiren.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lanying was foster mother to Dugu Shiren.

sentences.zh: 師仁父武都謀歸唐，王世充殺之。

translations.literal: Shiren's father Wudu plotted to return to Tang; Wang Shichong killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiren's father Wudu plotted to return to Tang. Wang Shichong killed him.

sentences.zh: 師仁始三歲，免死禁錮，蘭英請髡鉗得保養，許之。

translations.literal: Shiren was only three; spared death but imprisoned; Lanying begged to be tonsured and shackled to keep custody — it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiren was only three. Spared death but imprisoned. Lanying begged to be tonsured and shackled to keep custody — it was granted.

sentences.zh: 時喪亂，餓死者藉藉，遊丐道路以食師仁，身啖土飲水。

translations.literal: In those days of turmoil the dead lay piled; she begged along the roads to feed Shiren, herself eating earth and drinking water.
translations.idiomatic: In those days of turmoil the dead lay piled. She begged along the roads to feed Shiren, herself eating earth and drinking water.

sentences.zh: 後詐為采薪，竊師仁歸京師。

translations.literal: Later she feigned gathering firewood and stole Shiren away to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward she feigned gathering firewood and stole Shiren away to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其義，詔封蘭英永壽鄉君。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised her righteousness and decreed enfeoffment of Lanying as Lady of Yongshou Township.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu praised her righteousness and decreed enfeoffment of Lanying as Lady of Yongshou Township.

sentences.zh: 楊三安妻李，京兆高陵人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Yang San'an, was of Gaoling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang San'an's wife Li hailed from Gaoling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 舅姑亡，三安又死，子幼，孤窶，畫田夜紡，凡三年，葬舅姑及夫兄弟凡七喪，遠近嗟涕。

translations.literal: Parents-in-law died; San'an also died; the son was young; alone and destitute, she plowed by day and spun by night; in all three years she buried parents-in-law and seven of her husband's brothers — near and far wept.
translations.idiomatic: Parents-in-law died; San'an also died; the son was young; alone and destitute, she plowed by day and spun by night; in all three years she buried her parents-in-law and seven of her husband's brothers — people near and far wept for her.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而異之，賜帛三百段，遣州縣存問，免其徭役。

translations.literal: Taizong heard and marveled, bestowing three hundred bolts of silk, sending prefect and county to inquire, and exempting her from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong heard of it and marveled, bestowing three hundred bolts of silk, sending prefect and county to inquire, and exempting her from corvée.

sentences.zh: 樊會仁母敬，蒲州河東人，字象子。

translations.literal: Jing, mother of Fan Huiren, was of Hedong in Puzhou, courtesy name Xiangzi.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that jing, mother of Fan Huiren, was of Hedong in Puzhou, courtesy name Xiangzi.

sentences.zh: 笄而生會仁。

translations.literal: At hair-pinning age she bore Huiren.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age she bore Huiren.

sentences.zh: 夫死，事舅姑祥順。

translations.literal: When her husband died she served parents-in-law with gentle compliance.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died she served her parents-in-law with gentle compliance.

sentences.zh: 家以其少，俗嫁之，潛約婚於里人，至期，陽為母病，使歸視。

translations.literal: The family, seeing her youth, by custom wished to marry her off; she secretly betrothed to a man of the lane; when the day came she feigned her mother's illness and had her return to visit.
translations.idiomatic: The family, seeing her youth, by custom wished to marry her off. She secretly betrothed to a man of the lane. When the day came she feigned her mother's illness and had her return to visit.

sentences.zh: 敬至，知見紹，乃外為不知者，私謂會仁曰：「吾孀處不死者，以母老兒幼，今舅將奪吾志，汝云何？」

translations.literal: Jing arrived, saw the matchmaking, and outwardly acted as if unaware; privately she told Huiren: "I remain a widow and do not die because mother is old and the boy young; now the uncle-in-law will seize my resolve — what will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing arrived, saw the matchmaking, and outwardly acted as if unaware; privately she told Huiren: "I remain a widow and do not die because mother is old and the boy young; now the her uncle-in-law will seize my resolve — what will you do?"

sentences.zh: 會仁泣，敬曰：「兒毋啼！」

translations.literal: Huiren wept; Jing said: "Child, do not weep!"
translations.idiomatic: Huiren wept. Jing said: "Child, do not weep!"

sentences.zh: 乃伺隙遁去，家追及半道，以死自守，乃罷。

translations.literal: She then seized an opening and fled; the family pursued and overtook her halfway; she guarded her life by death-threat — they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: She then seized an opening and fled. The family pursued and overtook her halfway. She guarded her life by death-threat — they desisted.

sentences.zh: 會仁未冠卒，時敬母又終，既葬，謂所親曰：「母死子亡，何生為！」

translations.literal: Huiren died before the cap and sash; then Jing's mother also ended; after burial she said to kin: "Mother dead, son gone — why live!"
translations.idiomatic: Huiren died before the cap and sash. Then Jing's mother also ended. After burial she said to kin: "Mother dead, son gone — why live!"

sentences.zh: 不食數日死，聞者憐之。

translations.literal: She ate nothing for several days and died; hearers pitied her.
translations.idiomatic: She ate nothing for several days and died; those who heard pitied her her.

sentences.zh: 衛孝女，絳州夏人，字無忌。

translations.literal: The Filial Daughter of Wei, of Xia in Jiangzhou, courtesy name Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that the Filial Daughter of Wei, of Xia in Jiangzhou, courtesy name Wuji.

sentences.zh: 父為鄉人衛長則所殺，無忌甫六歲，無兄弟，母改嫁。

translations.literal: Her father was killed by Wei Changze of the village; Wuji was only six, with no brothers; her mother remarried.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was killed by Wei Changze of the village. Wuji was only six, with no brothers. Her mother remarried.

sentences.zh: 逮長，志報父仇。

translations.literal: When grown she resolved to avenge her father.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown, she set her heart on avenging her father.

sentences.zh: 會從父大延客，長則在坐，無忌抵以甓，殺之。

translations.literal: Once when her father's younger brother Yan greatly entertained guests, Changze was among them; Wuji struck him with a tile and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when her father's younger brother Yan greatly entertained guests, Changze was among them. Wuji struck him with a tile and killed him.

sentences.zh: 詣吏稱父冤已報，請就刑。

translations.literal: She went to the magistrate saying her father's wrong was already answered and asked to undergo punishment.
translations.idiomatic: She went to the district magistrate saying her father's wrong was already replied and asked to undergo punishment.

sentences.zh: 巡察使褚遂良以聞，太宗免其罪，給驛徙雍州，賜田宅。

translations.literal: Inspector Chu Suiliang reported it; Taizong pardoned her, gave post-horses, and moved her to Yongzhou, granting fields and a house.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Chu Suiliang reported it; Emperor Taizong pardoned her, gave post-horses, and moved her to Yongzhou, granting fields and a house.

sentences.zh: 州縣以禮嫁之。

translations.literal: Prefecture and county married her off with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and county gave her away in marriage with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 鄭義宗妻盧者，范陽士族也。

translations.literal: Lu, wife of Zheng Yizong, was of the gentry of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yizong's wife Lu hailed from the gentry of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 涉書史，事舅姑恭順。

translations.literal: She was versed in books and histories and served parents-in-law with respectful compliance.
translations.idiomatic: She was versed in books and histories and served her parents-in-law with respectful compliance.

sentences.zh: 夜有盜持兵劫其家，人皆匿竄，惟姑不能去，盧冒刃立姑側，為賊捽捶幾死。

translations.literal: At night robbers came armed and raided the house; all hid and fled — only the mother-in-law could not leave; Lu braved the blades and stood at her side, was seized and beaten nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: At night robbers came armed and raided the house; all hid and fled — only the her mother-in-law could not leave; Lu braved the blades and stood at her side, was seized and beaten nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 賊去，人問何為不懼，答曰：「人所以異鳥獸者，以其有仁義也。

translations.literal: When the robbers left, people asked why she was not afraid; she answered: "What distinguishes humans from birds and beasts is that they have benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the robbers left, people asked why she was not afraid. She answered: "What distinguishes humans from birds and beasts is that they have benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今憐里急難尚相赴，況姑可委棄邪？

translations.literal: Now in village distress people still rush to help one another — how much less may one abandon a mother-in-law?
translations.idiomatic: Now in village distress people still rush to help one another — how much less may one abandon a her mother-in-law?

sentences.zh: 若百有一危，我不得獨生。」

translations.literal: If there is one danger in a hundred, I cannot live alone.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that if there is one danger in a hundred, I cannot live alone.

sentences.zh: 姑曰：「歲寒然後知松柏後雕，吾乃今見婦之心。」

translations.literal: The mother-in-law said: "Only after bitter cold does one know the pine and cypress are last to wither — today I see the heart of a daughter-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: The her mother-in-law said: "Only after bitter cold does one know the pine and cypress are last to wither — today I see the heart of a daughter-in-law."

sentences.zh: 劉寂妻夏侯，滑州胙城人，字碎金。

translations.literal: Xiahou, wife of Liu Ji, of Zuocheng in Huazhou, courtesy name Suijin.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that xiahou, wife of Liu Ji, of Zuocheng in Huazhou, courtesy name Suijin.

sentences.zh: 父長雲為鹽城丞，喪明。

translations.literal: Her father Changyun was salt-city magistrate and lost his sight.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that her father Changyun was salt-city magistrate and lost his sight.

sentences.zh: 時劉已生二女矣，求與劉絕，歸侍父疾。

translations.literal: Liu had already borne two daughters; she asked to break with Liu and return to tend her father's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had already borne two daughters. She asked to break with Liu and return to tend her father's illness.

sentences.zh: 又事後母以孝稱。

translations.literal: She also served her stepmother and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: She also served her stepmother and won renown for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 五年父亡，毀不勝喪，被發徙跣，身負土作冢，廬其左，寒不綿、日一食者三年。

translations.literal: Five years later her father died; grief overwhelmed the mourning rites; she loosed her hair, went barefoot, carried earth herself to build the mound, and dwelt in a hut to the left — without cotton in cold, one meal a day — for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later her father died. Grief overwhelmed the mourning rites. She loosed her hair, went barefoot, carried earth herself to build the mound, and dwelt in a hut to the left — without cotton in cold, one meal a day — for three years.

sentences.zh: 詔賜物二十段、粟十石，表異門閭。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed twenty lengths of goods and ten piculs of grain, with a memorial to distinguish the gate.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that an edict bestowed twenty lengths of goods and ten piculs of grain, with a memorial to distinguish the gate.

sentences.zh: 後其女居母喪，亦如母行，官又賜粟帛，表其門。

translations.literal: Later when her daughter observed mourning for her mother she acted as her mother had; the office again bestowed grain and silk and marked the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later when her daughter observed mourning for her mother she acted as her mother had. The office again bestowed grain and silk and marked the gate.

sentences.zh: 于敏直妻張者，皖城公儉女也。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Yu Minzhi, was daughter of the Duke of Wancheng Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Minzhi's wife Zhang was a daughter of the Duke of Wancheng Jian.

sentences.zh: 生三歲，每父母病，已能晝夜省侍，顏色如成人。

translations.literal: At age three, whenever parents fell ill she could attend day and night with the composure of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that at age three, whenever parents fell ill she could attend day and night with the composure of an adult.

sentences.zh: 及長，愈恭順仁孝。

translations.literal: When grown she was yet more respectful, compliant, benevolent, and filial.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown she was yet more respectful, compliant, benevolent, and filial.

sentences.zh: 儉病篤，聞之，號泣幾絕。

translations.literal: When Jian was desperately ill and word reached her, she wailed until nearly dead.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jian was desperately ill and word reached her, she wailed until nearly dead.

sentences.zh: 儉死，一慟遂卒。

translations.literal: When Jian died, one great lament and she expired.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian perished, one great lament and she expired.

sentences.zh: 高宗懿其行，賜物百段，以狀屬史官。

translations.literal: Gaozong commended her conduct, bestowed a hundred lengths of goods, and sent the account to the historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong commended her conduct, bestowed a hundred lengths of goods, and sent the account to the historiographer.

sentences.zh: 楚王靈龜妃上官者，下邽士族也。

translations.literal: Shangguan, consort of Prince Linggui of Chu, was of the gentry of Xiaqi.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that shangguan, consort of Prince Linggui of Chu, was of the gentry of Xiaqi.

sentences.zh: 靈龜出繼哀王後，而舅姑在，妃朝夕侍奉，謹甚，凡珍美，非經獻不先嘗。

translations.literal: Linggui succeeded as heir to the Prince of Ai; parents-in-law still lived; the consort attended morning and evening with utmost care; whatever was rare and fine, unless presented in ritual she would not taste first.
translations.idiomatic: Linggui succeeded as heir to the Prince of Ai; her parents-in-law still lived; the consort attended morning and evening with utmost care; whatever was rare and fine, unless presented in ritual she would not taste first.

sentences.zh: 靈龜卒，將葬，前妃無近族，議者欲不舉，妃曰：「逝者有知，魂可無托乎？」

translations.literal: When Linggui died and was to be buried, the former consort had no near kin; deliberators wished not to bury together; the consort said: "If the departed have awareness, can the soul be without a resting place?"
translations.idiomatic: When Linggui died and was to be buried, the former consort had no near kin. Deliberators wished not to bury together. The consort said: "If the departed have awareness, can the soul be without a resting place?"

sentences.zh: 乃備禮合葬。

translations.literal: She then prepared rites for joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: She thereupon prepared rites for joint burial.

sentences.zh: 聞者嘉嘆。

translations.literal: Hearers praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard of it praised her and sighed with admiration.

sentences.zh: 喪除，兄弟共諭：「妃少，又無子，可不有行。」

translations.literal: When mourning ended, brothers together urged: "The consort is young and without sons — need she not go on?"
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, her brothers urged her together: "The consort is young and has no son—you need not remain a widow."

sentences.zh: 泣曰：「丈夫以義，婦人以節，我未能殉溝壑，尚可禦妝澤、祭他胙乎？」

translations.literal: She wept: "For a husband there is righteousness; for a woman there is constancy — I could not die in the ditch; can I still adorn myself and sacrifice at another's meat-offering?"
translations.idiomatic: She wept: "For a husband there is righteousness. For a woman there is constancy — I could not die in the ditch. Can I still adorn myself and sacrifice at another's meat-offering?"

sentences.zh: 將自劓刵，眾遂不敢強。

translations.literal: She was about to mutilate her face; the crowd dared not force her.
translations.idiomatic: She was about to mutilate her face. The crowd dared not force her.

sentences.zh: 楊紹宗妻王，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Yang Shaozong, was of Huayin in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shaozong's wife Wang hailed from Huayin in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 在褓而母亡，繼母鞠愛。

translations.literal: In swaddling clothes her mother died; the stepmother reared her with love.
translations.idiomatic: Still in swaddling clothes her mother died; the stepmother reared her with love.

sentences.zh: 父征遼歿，繼母又卒，王年十五，乃舉二母柩而立父象，招魂以葬，廬墓左。

translations.literal: Her father died campaigning in Liaodong; the stepmother also died; Wang at fifteen then raised both mothers' coffins and set up her father's image, summoned the soul for burial, and built a hut left of the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Her father died campaigning in Liaodong. The stepmother also died. Wang at fifteen then raised both mothers' coffins and set up her father's image, summoned the soul for burial, and built a hut left of the tomb.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，詔：「楊氏婦在隋時，父歿遼西，能招魂克葬。

translations.literal: In Yonghui an edict: "The woman of the Yang clan in Sui times — her father died in Liaoxi; she could summon the soul and complete burial.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui an edict: "The woman of the Yang clan in Sui times — her father died in Liaoxi. She could summon the soul and complete burial.

sentences.zh: 至祖父母塋隧，親服板築，哀感行路。」

translations.literal: At grandparents' tombs she personally wore mourning and pounded earth with a board — grief moved travelers on the road."
translations.idiomatic: At grandparents' tombs she personally wore mourning and pounded earth with a board—grief moved travelers on the road."

sentences.zh: 因賜物段並粟，以闕表門。

translations.literal: Therefore goods and grain were bestowed and a memorial gate set at the lane.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore goods and grain were bestowed and a memorial gate set at the lane," she said.

sentences.zh: 賈孝女，濮州鄄城人。

translations.literal: The Filial Daughter Jia, of Yuncheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, the Filial Daughter, was from Yuncheng in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 年十五，父為族人玄基所殺。

translations.literal: At fifteen her father was killed by clansman Xuanji.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen her father was slew by clansman Xuanji.

sentences.zh: 孝女弟強仁尚幼，孝女不肯嫁，躲撫育之。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Qiangren was still young; the Filial Daughter would not marry and secretly reared him.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Qiangren was still young; the filial daughter would not marry and secretly reared him.

sentences.zh: 強仁能自樹立，教伺玄基殺之，取其心告父墓。

translations.literal: When Qiangren could stand on his own she taught him to watch for Xuanji and kill him, taking his heart to report at their father's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that when Qiangren could stand on his own she taught him to watch for Xuanji and kill him, taking his heart to report at their father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 強仁詣縣言狀，有司論死。

translations.literal: Qiangren went to the county stating the facts; the authorities judged death.
translations.idiomatic: Qiangren went to the county stating the facts. The authorities judged death.

sentences.zh: 孝女詣闕請代弟死，高宗閔嘆，詔並免之，內徙洛陽。

translations.literal: The Filial Daughter went to the palace begging to die in her brother's stead; Gaozong pitied and sighed, issued an edict both pardoned, and moved them within to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Daughter went to the palace begging to die in her brother's stead; Emperor Gaozong pitied and sighed, issued an edict both pardoned, and moved them within to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李氏妻王阿足，深州鹿城人。

translations.literal: Wang Azu, wife of the Li clan, of Lucheng in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that wang Azu, wife of the Li clan, of Lucheng in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 早孤，無兄弟。

translations.literal: Early orphaned, without brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, she had no brothers.

sentences.zh: 歸李氏數歲，夫死無子，以嫠姊高年無供養，乃不忍嫁。

translations.literal: After several years with the Li clan the husband died without sons; her widowed elder sister was advanced in years without support — she could not bear to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: After several years with the Li clan the husband died without sons. Her widowed elder sister was advanced in years without support — she could not bear to remarry.

sentences.zh: 畫耕夜織，能辦生事，餘二十年，姊乃亡，葬送如禮。

translations.literal: She plowed by day and wove by night, could manage livelihood; for more than twenty years, then the sister died and burial and sending-off were as ritual.
translations.idiomatic: She plowed by day and wove by night, could manage livelihood. For more than twenty years, then the sister died and burial and sending-off were as ritual.

sentences.zh: 鄉人服其義，爭遣女妻往師其風訓。

translations.literal: Villagers admired her righteousness and vied to send daughters to marry there and learn her conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers admired her right conduct and vied to send daughters to marry there and learn her conduct.

sentences.zh: 壽終於家。

translations.literal: She died at home in old age.
translations.idiomatic: She died at home in her old age.

sentences.zh: 樊彥琛妻魏者，揚州人。

translations.literal: Wei, wife of Fan Yanchen, was of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanchen's wife Wei hailed from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥琛病，魏曰：「公病且篤，不忍公獨死。」

translations.literal: Yanchen fell ill; Wei said: "Sir's illness is already desperate — I cannot bear that you die alone."
translations.idiomatic: Yanchen fell ill. Wei said: "Sir's illness is already desperate — I cannot bear that you die alone."

sentences.zh: 彥琛曰：「死生，常道也。

translations.literal: Yanchen said: "Life and death are the constant way.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchen said: "Life and death are the constant way," she said.

sentences.zh: 幸養諸孤使成立，相從而死，非吾取也。」

translations.literal: Fortune the orphans to maturity; to follow and die is not what I choose."
translations.idiomatic: Fortune the orphans to maturity. To follow and die is not what I choose."

sentences.zh: 彥琛卒，值徐敬業難，陷兵中。

translations.literal: When Yanchen died, Xu Jingye's rebellion arose; she fell among the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanchen died, Xu Jingye's rebellion arose. She fell among the troops.

sentences.zh: 聞其知音，令鼓箏，魏曰：「夫亡不死，而逼我管弦，禍由我發。」

translations.literal: Hearing she knew music, they ordered her to play the zither; Wei said: "My husband dead and I not dead — yet you force strings upon me; disaster springs from me."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing she knew music, they ordered her to play the zither. Wei said: "My husband dead and I not dead — yet you force strings upon me. Disaster springs from me."

sentences.zh: 引刀斬其指。

translations.literal: She drew a knife and cut off her finger.
translations.idiomatic: She drew a knife and cut off her finger," she said.

sentences.zh: 軍伍欲強妻之，固拒不從，乃妨擬頸曰：「從我者不死。」

translations.literal: The soldiers wished to force her as wife; she firmly refused; they then held a blade to her neck saying: "Obey me and you will not die."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers wished to force her as wife. She firmly refused. They then held a blade to her neck saying: "Obey me and you will not die."

sentences.zh: 魏厲聲曰：「狗盜，乃欲辱人，速死，吾志也！」

translations.literal: Wei cried harshly: "Dog-thief — you would shame a person; die quickly — that is my will!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei cried harshly: "Dog-thief — you would shame a person. Die quickly — that is my will!"

sentences.zh: 乃見害，聞者傷之。

translations.literal: She was then killed; hearers grieved.
translations.idiomatic: She was then killed; those who heard grieved for her.

sentences.zh: 李畬母者，失其氏。

translations.literal: The mother of Li Yu — her clan name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The mother of Li Yu—her clan name is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 有淵識。

translations.literal: She had deep discernment.
translations.idiomatic: She possessed keen discernment.

sentences.zh: 畬為監察御史，得稟米，量之三斛而贏，問於史，曰：「御史米，不概也。」

translations.literal: Yu was investigating censor; he received ration rice, measured three hu and it overflowed; he asked the clerk, who said: "Censors' rice is not leveled."
translations.idiomatic: Yu was investigating censor. He received ration rice, measured three hu and it overflowed. He asked the clerk, who said: "Censors' rice is not leveled."

sentences.zh: 又問車庸有幾，曰：「御史不償也。」

translations.literal: He asked how many cart fees there were; the answer: "Censors do not pay."
translations.idiomatic: He asked how many cart fees there were. The answer: "Censors do not pay."

sentences.zh: 母怒，敕歸餘米，償其庸，因切責畬。

translations.literal: Mother was angry, ordered the surplus rice returned and fees paid, and sharply reproved Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Mother was angry, ordered the surplus rice returned and fees paid, and sharply reproved Yu," she said.

sentences.zh: 畬劾倉官，自言狀，諸御史聞之，有慚色。

translations.literal: Yu impeached the granary officer, confessed his own case; all investigating censors hearing it showed shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yu impeached the granary officer, confessed his own case. All investigating censors hearing it showed shame.

sentences.zh: 汴女李者，年八歲父亡，殯於堂十年，朝夕臨。

translations.literal: Li of Bian — at eight her father died; the coffin remained in the hall ten years; morning and evening she attended.
translations.idiomatic: Li of Bian — at eight her father died. The coffin remained in the hall ten years. Morning and evening she attended.

sentences.zh: 及笄，母欲嫁之。

translations.literal: At hair-pinning her mother wished to marry her off.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age her mother wished to marry her off.

sentences.zh: 斷髪，丐終養。

translations.literal: She cut her hair and begged to end her life in service.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that she cut her hair and begged to end her life in service.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，哀號過人，自庀葬具，州里送葬千餘人。

translations.literal: In mourning for her mother her wailing surpassed others; she herself prepared burial goods; more than a thousand in the district escorted the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for her mother her wailing surpassed others. She herself prepared burial goods. More than a thousand in the district escorted the funeral.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓，蓬頭，跣而負土，以完園塋，蒔松數百。

translations.literal: She built a hut at the tomb, unkempt hair, barefoot carrying earth to complete the garden mound, planting several hundred pines.
translations.idiomatic: She built a hut at the tomb, unkempt hair, barefoot carrying earth to complete the garden mound, planting a number of hundred pines.

sentences.zh: 武後時，按察使薛季昶表之，詔樹闕門閭。

translations.literal: In Wu Hou's time investigating commissioner Xue Jichang memorialized her; an edict set a memorial gate at the lane.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's time investigating commissioner Xue Jichang submitted a memorial her; an edict set a memorial gate at the lane.

sentences.zh: 崔繪妻盧者，鸞臺侍郎獻之女。

translations.literal: Lu, wife of Cui Hui, was daughter of Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hui's wife Lu was a daughter of Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace Xian.

sentences.zh: 獻有美名。

translations.literal: Xian had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xian enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 繪喪，盧年少，家欲嫁之，盧稱疾不許。

translations.literal: When Hui died Lu was young; the family wished to marry her; Lu claimed illness and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died Lu was young. The family wished to marry her. Lu claimed illness and would not consent.

sentences.zh: 女兄適工部侍郎李思沖，早亡。

translations.literal: Her elder sister had married Vice Minister of Works Li Sichong, who died early.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister had married Vice Minister of Works Li Sichong, who perished early.

sentences.zh: 思沖方顯重，表求繼室，詔許，家內外姻皆然可。

translations.literal: Sichong was then prominent; he memorialized seeking a successor wife; the edict granted it; family and affines inside and out all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Sichong was then prominent; he submitted a memorial seeking a successor wife; the edict granted it; family and affines inside and out all approved.

sentences.zh: 思沖歸幣三百輿，盧不可，曰：「吾豈再辱於人乎？

translations.literal: Sichong sent betrothal gifts in three hundred carts; Lu would not accept, saying: "How could I be shamed twice by men?
translations.idiomatic: Sichong sent betrothal gifts in three hundred carts. Lu would not accept, saying: "How could I be shamed twice by men?

sentences.zh: 寧沒身為婢。」

translations.literal: Better to end my life as a serving woman."
translations.idiomatic: So it was that better to end my life as a serving woman."

sentences.zh: 是夕，出自竇，糞穢蔑面，還崔舍，斷發自誓。

translations.literal: That night she came out through a hole, smeared dung on her face, returned to the Cui house, cut her hair and swore.
translations.idiomatic: That night she came out through a hole, smeared dung on her face, returned to the Cui house, cut her hair and swore," she said.

sentences.zh: 思沖以聞，武後不奪也，詔為浮屠尼以終。

translations.literal: Sichong reported it; Wu Hou did not compel her and issued an edict she become a Buddhist nun to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Sichong reported it; Empress Wu did not compel her and issued an edict she become a Buddhist nun to the end.

sentences.zh: 堅貞節婦李者，年十七，嫁為鄭廉妻。

translations.literal: Li the steadfast chaste wife — at seventeen she married Zheng Lian as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Li the steadfast chaste wife—at seventeen she married Zheng Lian as wife.

sentences.zh: 未逾年，廉死，常布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: Before a year Lian died; she always wore plain cloth and coarse food.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year Lian died. She always wore plain cloth and coarse food.

sentences.zh: 夜忽夢男子求為妻，初不許，後數數夢之。

translations.literal: At night she suddenly dreamed a man asked to be her husband; at first she did not consent; later he dreamed repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: At night she suddenly dreamed a man asked to be her husband. At first she did not consent. Later he dreamed repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 李自疑容貌未衰鬼所召也，即截發，麻衣，不薰飾，垢面塵膚，自是不復夢。

translations.literal: Li suspected her looks were not yet faded and ghosts summoned her; she then cut her hair, wore hemp, used no perfume, filthy face and dusty skin — from then no more dreams.
translations.idiomatic: Li suspected her looks were not yet faded and ghosts summoned her. She then cut her hair, wore hemp, used no perfume, filthy face and dusty skin — from then no more dreams.

sentences.zh: 刺史白大威欽其操，號堅貞節婦，表旌門闕，名所居曰節婦里。

translations.literal: Prefect Bai Dawei admired her conduct, styled her the steadfast chaste wife, memorialized a gate and memorial tower, naming her dwelling Chaste Wife Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Bai Dawei admired her conduct, styled her the steadfast chaste wife, submitted a memorial a gate and memorial tower, naming her dwelling Chaste Wife Lane.

sentences.zh: 符鳳妻某氏，字玉英，尤姝美。

translations.literal: A certain clan, wife of Fu Feng, courtesy name Yuying, exceptionally beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that a certain clan, wife of Fu Feng, courtesy name Yuying, exceptionally beautiful.

sentences.zh: 鳳以罪徙儋州，至南海，為獠賊所殺，脅玉英私之，對曰：「一婦人不足事眾男子，請推一長者。」

translations.literal: Feng was punished and exiled to Danzhou; reaching the Southern Sea he was killed by Liao bandits who forced Yuying to private union; she answered: "One woman is not enough to serve many men — please choose one elder."
translations.idiomatic: Feng was punished and exiled to Danzhou. Reaching the Southern Sea he was killed by Liao bandits who forced Yuying to private union. She answered: "One woman is not enough to serve many men — please choose one elder."

sentences.zh: 賊然之。

translations.literal: The bandits agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃請更衣，有頃，盛服立於舟，罵曰：「受賊辱，不如死！」

translations.literal: She then asked to change clothes; presently, in full dress she stood on the boat and cursed: "To suffer bandit shame is worse than death!"
translations.idiomatic: She then asked to change clothes. Presently, in full dress she stood on the boat and cursed: "To suffer bandit shame is worse than death!"

sentences.zh: 自沈於海。

translations.literal: She threw herself into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into the sea," she said.

sentences.zh: 高叡妻秦。

translations.literal: Qin, wife of Gao Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was wife to Gao Rui.

sentences.zh: 叡為趙州刺史，為默啜所攻。

translations.literal: Rui was prefect of Zhao; he was attacked by Mohe chieftain Mokusho.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was prefect of Zhao. He was attacked by Mohe chieftain Mokusho.

sentences.zh: 州陷，叡仰藥不死，至默啜所，示以竇帶異袍，曰：「降我，賜爾官；

translations.literal: The prefecture fell; Rui took poison but did not die; brought to Mokusho's place he was shown a brocade belt and strange robe, saying: "Submit to me and I grant you office;
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture fell. Rui took poison but did not die. Brought to Mokusho's place he was shown a brocade belt and strange robe, saying: "Submit to me and I grant you office.

sentences.zh: 不降，且死。」

translations.literal: if not, then death."
translations.idiomatic: Refuse, and death follows."

sentences.zh: 叡視秦，秦曰：「君受天子恩，當以死報，賊一品官安足榮？」

translations.literal: Rui looked at Qin; Qin said: "You received the Son of Heaven's grace — you should repay with death; what glory is a bandit's first-rank office?"
translations.idiomatic: Rui looked at Qin. Qin said: "You received the Son of Heaven's grace — you should repay with death. What glory is a bandit's first-rank office?"

sentences.zh: 自是皆瞑目不語。

translations.literal: From then both closed eyes and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: From then both closed eyes and spoke no more," she said.

sentences.zh: 默啜知不可屈，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Mokusho knew they could not be bent and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Mokusho saw they could not be bent to his will and had them killed.

sentences.zh: 王琳妻韋者，士族也。

translations.literal: Wei, wife of Wang Lin, was of the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin's wife Wei hailed from the gentry.

sentences.zh: 琳為眉州司功參軍，俗僭侈盛飾，韋不知有簪珥。

translations.literal: Lin was merit officer of Meizhou; custom was extravagant ornament; Wei knew nothing of hairpins and ear ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was merit officer of Meizhou. Custom was extravagant ornament. Wei knew nothing of hairpins and ear ornaments.

sentences.zh: 訓二子堅、冰有法，後皆名聞。

translations.literal: She trained the two sons Jian and Bing with method; both later were famed.
translations.idiomatic: She trained the two sons Jian and Bing with method. Both later were famed.

sentences.zh: 琳卒時，韋年二十五，家欲強嫁之，韋固拒，至不聽音樂，處一室，或終日不食。

translations.literal: When Lin died Wei was twenty-five; the family wished to force remarriage; Wei firmly refused, even not hearing music, dwelling in one room, sometimes not eating all day.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin died Wei was twenty-five. The family wished to force remarriage. Wei firmly refused, even not hearing music, dwelling in one room, sometimes not eating all day.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十五，著《女訓》行於世。

translations.literal: She died at seventy-five; her Instructions for Women circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: She died at seventy-five. Her Instructions for Women circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 盧惟清妻徐，淄州人，世客陳留。

translations.literal: Xu, wife of Lu Weiqing, was of Zizhou; the clan sojourned in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, wife of Lu Weiqing, was of Zizhou. The clan sojourned in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 惟清仕歷校書郎。

translations.literal: Weiqing served as proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing held the post of proofreader.

sentences.zh: 徐女兄之夫李宜得以罪斥，惟清坐僚姻，貶播川尉。

translations.literal: Xu's elder sister's husband Li Yide was dismissed for crime; Weiqing sat as colleague by marriage and was demoted to Bochuan district aide.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's elder sister's husband Li Yide was dismissed for crime. Weiqing sat as colleague by marriage and was demoted to Bochuan district aide.

sentences.zh: 徐還鄉里，糲食，斥鉛膏，采絺不禦。

translations.literal: Xu returned to her village, coarse food, rejecting lead cosmetics, gathering ramie cloth without fine dress.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that xu returned to her village, coarse food, rejecting lead cosmetics, gathering ramie cloth without fine dress.

sentences.zh: 會大赦，徐間關迎惟清，至荊州，聞惟清死，二髯奴將劫徐歸下江，徐知之，數其罪，奴不敢逼，劫其貲去。

translations.literal: When a great amnesty came, Xu by hard paths went to meet Weiqing; at Jingzhou she heard Weiqing had died; two bearded slaves would seize Xu and take her downriver; Xu knew it, counted their crimes; the slaves dared not press, robbed her goods and left.
translations.idiomatic: When a great amnesty came, Xu by hard paths went to meet Weiqing. At Jingzhou she heard Weiqing had died. Two bearded slaves would seize Xu and take her downriver. Xu knew it, counted their crimes. The slaves dared not press, robbed her goods and left.

sentences.zh: 徐倍道行至播川，足繭流血，得惟清戶，以喪還，閱歲至洛陽。

translations.literal: Xu doubled her pace to Bochuan; feet blistered and bled; she obtained Weiqing's household and returned with the coffin; within a year she reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu doubled her pace to Bochuan. Feet blistered and bled. She obtained Weiqing's household and returned with the coffin. Within a year she reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 既葬，以無子，終服還陳留。

translations.literal: After burial, having no sons, she completed mourning and returned to Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that after burial, having no sons, she completed mourning and returned to Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 汴州刺史齊瀚高其節，頌而詩之。

translations.literal: Bianzhou prefect Qi Han exalted her constancy and composed verse in praise.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that bianzhou prefect Qi Han exalted her constancy and composed verse in praise.

sentences.zh: 饒娥字瓊真，饒州樂平人。

translations.literal: Rao E, courtesy name Qiongzhen, of Leping in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rao E of Leping in Raozhou, courtesy name Qiongzhen.

sentences.zh: 生小家，勤織纴，頗自修整。

translations.literal: Born to a small household, diligent at weaving, quite self-disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that born to a small household, diligent at weaving, quite self-disciplined.

sentences.zh: 父勣，漁於江，遇風濤，舟覆，屍不出。

translations.literal: Her father Ji fished on the river; encountering wind and waves the boat capsized; the corpse did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Ji fished on the river. Encountering wind and waves the boat capsized. The corpse did not emerge.

sentences.zh: 娥年十四，哭水上，不食三日死。

translations.literal: E at fourteen cried on the water, ate nothing for three days and died.
translations.idiomatic: E at fourteen cried out on the water, ate nothing for three days and perished.

sentences.zh: 俄大震電，水蟲多死，父屍浮出，鄉人異之，歸赗具禮，葬父及娥鄱水之陰。

translations.literal: Soon great thunder and lightning; water creatures mostly died; her father's corpse floated up; villagers marveled, returned gifts with full rites, burying father and E on the north bank of the Po River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon great thunder and lightning. Water creatures mostly died. Her father's corpse floated up. Villagers marveled, returned gifts with full rites, burying father and E on the north bank of the Po River.

sentences.zh: 縣令魏仲光碣其墓。

translations.literal: Magistrate Wei Zhongguang inscribed her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that magistrate Wei Zhongguang inscribed her tomb.

sentences.zh: 建中初，黜陟使鄭淑則表旌其閭，河東柳宗元為立碑云。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianzhong investigating commissioner Zheng Shuzhe memorialized her lane; Hedong Liu Zongyuan erected a stele.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianzhong investigating commissioner Zheng Shuzhe submitted a memorial her lane; Hedong Liu Zongyuan erected a stele.

sentences.zh: 竇伯女、仲女，京兆奉天人。

translations.literal: The elder and younger daughters of Dou, of Fengtian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that the elder and younger daughters of Dou, of Fengtian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，遇賊行剽，二女自匿山谷，賊跡而得之，將逼以私。

translations.literal: In Yongtai they met bandits raiding on the road; the two girls hid in mountain valleys; the bandits tracked and found them, about to force private union.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai they met bandits raiding on the road. The two girls hid in mountain valleys. The bandits tracked and found them, about to force private union.

sentences.zh: 行臨大谷，伯曰：「我豈受汙於賊！」

translations.literal: Walking to a great valley the elder said: "How could I suffer defilement from bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Walking to a great valley the elder said: "How could I suffer defilement from rebels!"

sentences.zh: 乃自投下，賊大駭。

translations.literal: She then threw herself down; the bandits were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: She then threw herself down. The bandits were greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 俄而仲亦躍而墜。

translations.literal: Presently the younger also leaped and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the younger also leaped and fell.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹第五琦表其烈行，詔旌門閭，免其家徭役，官為庀葬。

translations.literal: Jingzhao intendant Di Wuqi memorialized their fierce conduct; an edict marked the gate, exempted the family from corvée, and the office prepared burial.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao intendant Di Wuqi submitted a memorial their fierce conduct; an edict marked the gate, exempted the family from corvée, and the office prepared burial.

sentences.zh: 盧甫妻李，秦州成紀人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Lu Fu, of Chenji in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that li, wife of Lu Fu, of Chenji in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 父瀾，永泰初為蘄令。

translations.literal: Her father Lan, at the start of Yongtai was magistrate of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that her father Lan, at the start of Yongtai was magistrate of Qi.

sentences.zh: 梁、宋兵興，瀾諭降劇賊數千人。

translations.literal: Liang and Song armies rose; Lan persuaded and induced fierce bandits numbering thousands to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Song armies rose. Lan persuaded and induced fierce bandits numbering thousands to submit.

sentences.zh: 刺史曹升襲賊，敗之。

translations.literal: Prefect Cao Sheng attacked the bandits and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cao Sheng attacked the rebels and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 賊疑瀾賣己，執瀾及其弟渤，兄弟爭相代死，李見父被殷，亦請代父，遂皆遇害。

translations.literal: The bandits suspected Lan had sold them; they seized Lan and his younger brother Bo; the brothers vied to die in one another's stead; Li seeing her father bound also asked to replace her father — all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits suspected Lan had sold them. They seized Lan and his younger brother Bo. The brothers vied to die in one another's stead. Li seeing her father bound also asked to replace her father — all were killed.

sentences.zh: 又有王泛妻裴者，亦俘賊中，欲汙之，罵曰：「吾，衣冠子，豈愛生受汙邪！」

translations.literal: There was also Pei, wife of Wang Fan, also captive among bandits; they wished to defile her; she cursed: "I am a cap-and-gown child's wife — how could I love life and suffer shame!"
translations.idiomatic: There was also Pei, wife of Wang Fan, also captive among bandits. They wished to defile her. She cursed: "I am a cap-and-gown child's wife — how could I love life and suffer shame!"

sentences.zh: 賊臨以兵，罵不止，乃支解焉。

translations.literal: The bandits faced her with weapons; she cursed without cease — they dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits faced her with weapons. She cursed without cease — they dismembered her.

sentences.zh: 宣慰使李季卿聞狀，詔贈李者昌縣君、裴河東縣君，瀾、渤並贈官。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Li Jiqing heard the facts; an edict posthumously enfeoffed Li as Lady of Chang county and Pei as Lady of Hedong; Lan and Bo both received posthumous offices.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Li Jiqing heard the facts. An edict posthumously enfeoffed Li as Lady of Chang county and Pei as Lady of Hedong. Lan and Bo both received posthumous offices.

sentences.zh: 鄒待征妻薄者，從侍征官江陰。

translations.literal: Bo, wife of Zou Daizheng, followed Daizheng in office at Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that bo, wife of Zou Daizheng, followed Daizheng in office at Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 袁晁亂，薄為賊所掠，將汙之，不從。

translations.literal: Yuan Chao rebelled; Bo was seized by bandits who would defile her; she would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chao rebelled. Bo was seized by bandits who would defile her. She would not submit.

sentences.zh: 語家媼使報待征曰：「我義不辱。」

translations.literal: She told the household matron to report to Daizheng: "I would die before shame."
translations.idiomatic: So it was that she told the household matron to report to Daizheng: "I would die before shame."

sentences.zh: 即死於水。

translations.literal: She then died in the water.
translations.idiomatic: She thereupon perished in the water.

sentences.zh: 賊去，得其屍。

translations.literal: The bandits left; her corpse was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits withdrew, her body was recovered.

sentences.zh: 義聲動江南，聞人李華作《哀節婦賦》。

translations.literal: Righteous fame moved Jiangnan; the man of letters Li Hua composed Lament for the Chaste Wife.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous fame moved Jiangnan. The man of letters Li Hua composed Lament for the Chaste Wife.

sentences.zh: 金節婦者，安南賊帥陶齊亮之母也。

translations.literal: The Golden Chaste Wife was mother of Annan bandit chief Tao Qiliang.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that the Golden Chaste Wife was mother of Annan bandit chief Tao Qiliang.

sentences.zh: 常以忠義誨齊亮，頑不受，遂絕之。

translations.literal: She always admonished Qiliang with loyalty and righteousness; stubbornly he would not receive it — she broke with him.
translations.idiomatic: She always admonished Qiliang with loyalty and righteousness. Stubbornly he would not receive it — she broke with him.

sentences.zh: 自田而食，紡而衣，州里矜法焉。

translations.literal: She tilled for food and spun for clothing; the district admired and took her as model.
translations.idiomatic: She tilled for food and spun for clothing. The district admired and took her as model.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，詔賜兩丁侍養，本道使四時存問終身。

translations.literal: At the start of Dali an edict granted two corvée servants for support; the circuit commissioner inquired four seasons for life.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dali an edict granted two corvée servants for support. The circuit commissioner inquired four seasons for life.

sentences.zh: 高湣女名妹妹，父彥昭事李正己。

translations.literal: The daughter of Gao Min was named Meimei; her father Yanzhao served Li Zhengyi.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Gao Min was named Meimei. Her father Yanzhao served Li Zhengyi.

sentences.zh: 及納拒命，質其妻子，使守濮陽。

translations.literal: When Na resisted orders his wife and children were held hostage, made to guard Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Na resisted orders his wife and children were held hostage, made to guard Puyang.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，挈城歸河南都統劉玄佐，納屠其家。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong she led the city back to Henan chief Liu Xuanzuo; Na slaughtered her family.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong she led the city back to Henan chief Liu Xuanzuo. Na slaughtered her family.

sentences.zh: 時女七歲，母李憐其幼，請免死為婢，許之。

translations.literal: The girl was then seven; mother Li pitied her youth and begged spare her life as serving woman — it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The girl was then seven. Mother Li pitied her youth and begged spare her life as serving woman — it was granted.

sentences.zh: 女不肯，曰：「母兄皆不免，何賴而生？」

translations.literal: The girl would not consent, saying: "Mother and elder brother all cannot be spared — on what could I rely to live?"
translations.idiomatic: The girl refused to consent, saying: "Mother and elder brother all cannot be spared — on what could I rely to live?"

sentences.zh: 母兄將被刑，遍拜四方。

translations.literal: When mother and brother were about to be executed they bowed in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: When mother and brother were on the verge of be executed they bowed in all directions.

sentences.zh: 女問故，答曰：「神可祈也。」

translations.literal: The girl asked the reason; they answered: "The spirits may be prayed to."
translations.idiomatic: The girl asked the reason. They answered: "The spirits may be prayed to."

sentences.zh: 女曰：「我家以忠義誅，神尚何知而拜之！」

translations.literal: The girl said: "Our house is executed for loyalty and righteousness — what do spirits know that we bow!"
translations.idiomatic: The girl said: "Our house is executed for loyalty and right conduct — what do spirits know that we bow!"

sentences.zh: 問父在所，西向哭，再拜就死。

translations.literal: She asked where her father was, cried westward, bowed twice and went to death.
translations.idiomatic: She asked where her father was, cried out westward, bowed twice and went to death.

sentences.zh: 德宗駭嘆，詔太常謚曰湣。

translations.literal: Suzong was startled and sighed; issued an edict the Director of Ceremonies to posthumous title Min.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was startled and sighed; issued an edict the Director of Ceremonies to posthumous title Min.

sentences.zh: 諸儒爭為之誄。

translations.literal: Scholars vied to compose dirges.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars competed to write dirges for her.

sentences.zh: 彥昭從玄佐救寧陵，復汴州，累功授潁州刺史。

translations.literal: Yanzhao followed Xuanzuo to rescue Ningling, recovered Bianzhou, accumulated merit and was appointed prefect of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that yanzhao followed Xuanzuo to rescue Ningling, recovered Bianzhou, accumulated merit and was appointed prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 朝廷錄其忠，居州二十年不徙，卒贈陜州都督。

translations.literal: The court recorded his loyalty; he held the prefecture twenty years without transfer; at death posthumously made Area Commander of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The court recorded his loyalty. He held the prefecture twenty years without transfer. At death posthumously made Area Commander of Shan.

sentences.zh: 楊烈婦者，李侃妻也。

translations.literal: The Fierce Wife Yang was wife of Li Kan.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that the Fierce Wife Yang was wife of Li Kan.

sentences.zh: 建中末，李希烈陷汴，謀襲陳州。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong Li Xilie took Bian and plotted to strike Chen.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that at the end of Jianzhong Li Xilie took Bian and plotted to strike Chen.

sentences.zh: 侃為項城令，希烈分兵數千略定諸縣，侃以城小賊銳，欲逃去，婦曰：「寇至當守，力不足，則死焉。

translations.literal: Kan was magistrate of Xiangcheng; Xilie sent several thousand troops to subdue the counties; Kan, the city small and the bandits sharp, wished to flee; the wife said: "When bandits come one must defend; strength insufficient — then die.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was magistrate of Xiangcheng. Xilie sent several thousand troops to subdue the counties. Kan, the city small and the bandits sharp, wished to flee. The wife said: "When bandits come one must defend. Strength insufficient — then die.

sentences.zh: 君而逃，尚誰守？」

translations.literal: You flee — who will defend?"
translations.idiomatic: If you flee, who will defend the city?"

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「兵少財乏，若何？」

translations.literal: Kan said: "Few troops, scarce funds — what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan said: "Few troops, scarce funds — what then??" she asked."

sentences.zh: 婦曰：「縣不守，則地賊地也，倉廩府庫皆其積也，百姓皆其戰士也於國家何有？

translations.literal: The wife said: "If the county is not held, the land is bandit land; granaries and treasuries are their stores; the people are their warriors — what is left to the state?
translations.idiomatic: The wife said: "If the county is not held, the land is bandit land. Granaries and treasuries are their stores. The people are their warriors — what is left to the state?

sentences.zh: 請重賞募死士，尚可濟。」

translations.literal: Please heavily reward and recruit dare-to-die men — it may yet be saved."
translations.idiomatic: Please heavily reward and recruit dare-to-die men—it may yet be saved."

sentences.zh: 侃乃召吏民入廷中曰：「令誠若主也，然滿歲則去，非如吏民生此土也，墳墓存焉，宜相與死守，忍失身北面奉賊乎？」

translations.literal: Kan then summoned clerks and people into the hall saying: "The magistrate is truly like a lord — yet when the year ends he departs, not like clerks and people born on this soil; tombs remain here — you should together die in defense — can you bear to lose yourselves facing north serving bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan then summoned clerks and people into the hall saying: "The magistrate is truly like a lord — yet when the year ends he departs, not like clerks and people born on this soil. Tombs remain here — you should together die in defense — can you bear to lose yourselves facing north serving bandits?"

sentences.zh: 眾泣，許諾。

translations.literal: The crowd wept and promised.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd wept and promised," she said.

sentences.zh: 乃徇曰：「以瓦石擊賊者，賞千錢；

translations.literal: He then proclaimed: "Who strikes bandits with tile and stone — reward a thousand cash;
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon proclaimed: "Who strikes bandits with tile and stone — reward a thousand cash;

sentences.zh: 以刀矢殺賊者，萬錢。」

translations.literal: who kills bandits with blade and arrow — ten thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: who kills rebels with blade and arrow — ten thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 得數百人。

translations.literal: He got several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He got a number of hundred men.

sentences.zh: 侃率以乘城，婦身自釁以享眾。

translations.literal: Kan led them to mount the walls; the wife personally smeared blood to feast the host.
translations.idiomatic: Kan led them to mount the walls. The wife personally smeared blood to feast the host.

sentences.zh: 報賊曰：「項城父老義不下賊，得吾城不足為威，宜亟去；

translations.literal: They reported to the bandits: "The elders of Xiangcheng in righteousness will not submit to bandits — taking our city is insufficient for prestige; you should quickly go;
translations.idiomatic: They reported to the bandits: "The elders of Xiangcheng in righteousness will not submit to bandits — taking our city is insufficient for prestige. You should quickly go.

sentences.zh: 徒失利，無益也。」

translations.literal: you will only lose advantage, without benefit."
translations.idiomatic: You will only forfeit advantage, with no gain."

sentences.zh: 賊大笑。

translations.literal: The bandits laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels laughed greatly.

sentences.zh: 侃中流矢，還家，婦責曰：「君不在，人誰肯固？

translations.literal: Kan was struck by a flying arrow, returned home; the wife reproached: "You not present — who will hold firm?
translations.idiomatic: Kan was struck by a flying arrow, returned home. The wife reproached: "You not present — who will hold firm?

sentences.zh: 死於外，猶愈於狀也。」

translations.literal: To die outside is still better than this posture."
translations.idiomatic: So it was that to die outside is still better than this posture."

sentences.zh: 侃遽登城。

translations.literal: Kan hastened to mount the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Kan hastened to mount the walls," she said.

sentences.zh: 會賊將中矢死，遂引去，縣卒完。

translations.literal: When the bandit general was struck by arrow and died, they then withdrew; the county was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: When an arrow struck the bandit general and killed him, the raiders withdrew and the county was saved whole.

sentences.zh: 詔遷侃太平令。

translations.literal: An edict moved Kan to magistrate of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred Kan to be magistrate of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 先是萬歲通天初，契丹寇平州，鄒保英為刺史，城且陷，妻奚率家僮女丁乘城，不下賊，詔封誠節夫人。

translations.literal: Earlier at the start of Wansui tongtian the Khitan raided Pingzhou; Zou Baoying was prefect; the city about to fall; his wife Xi led household retainers and women to mount the walls and would not yield to bandits; an edict enfeoffed her Lady of Sincere Constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at the start of Wansui tongtian the Khitan raided Pingzhou. Zou Baoying was prefect. The city about to fall. His wife Xi led household retainers and women to mount the walls and would not yield to bandits. An edict enfeoffed her Lady of Sincere Constancy.

sentences.zh: 默啜攻飛狐，縣令古玄應妻高能固守，虜引去，詔封徇忠縣君。

translations.literal: Mokusho attacked Feihu; magistrate Gu Xuanying's wife Gao Neng firmly held; the barbarians withdrew; an edict enfeoffed her Lady of Xunzhong county.
translations.idiomatic: Mokusho attacked Feihu. Magistrate Gu Xuanying's wife Gao Neng firmly held. The barbarians withdrew. An edict enfeoffed her Lady of Xunzhong county.

sentences.zh: 史思明之叛，衛州女子侯、滑州女子唐、青州女子王，相與歃血赴行營討賊，滑濮節度使許叔冀表其忠，皆補果毅。

translations.literal: In Shi Siming's rebellion the women Hou of Weizhou, Tang of Huazhou, and Wang of Qingzhou together swore blood and went to the campaigning army to attack bandits; Huai-Pu military commissioner Xu Shuji memorialized their loyalty — all were made resolute guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Shi Siming's rebellion the women Hou of Weizhou, Tang of Huazhou, and Wang of Qingzhou together swore blood and went to the campaigning army to attack bandits; Huai-Pu military commissioner Xu Shuji submitted a memorial their loyalty — all were made resolute guards.

sentences.zh: 雖敢決不忘於國，然不如楊烈婦慨慷知君臣大義云。

translations.literal: Though daring and not forgetting the state, yet they are not like the Fierce Wife Yang, magnanimous and knowing the great righteousness of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Though daring and not forgetting the state, yet they are not like the fierce wife Yang, magnanimous and knowing the great righteousness of ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 賈直言妻董。

translations.literal: Dong, wife of Jia Zhiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong was wife to Jia Zhiyan.

sentences.zh: 直言坐事，貶嶺南，以妻少，乃訣曰：「生死不可期，吾去，可亟嫁，無須也。」

translations.literal: Zhiyan sat in crime and was demoted to Lingnan; seeing his wife young he took leave saying: "Life and death cannot be foreseen; I go — you may quickly remarry; do not wait."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyan sat in crime and was demoted to Lingnan. Seeing his wife young he took leave saying: "Life and death cannot be foreseen. I go — you may quickly remarry. Do not wait."

sentences.zh: 董不答，引繩束發，封以帛，使直言署，曰：「非君手不解。」

translations.literal: Dong did not answer; drew cord and bound her hair, sealed it in silk, had Zhiyan sign, saying: "Not opened except by your hand."
translations.idiomatic: Dong did not answer. Drew cord and bound her hair, sealed it in silk, had Zhiyan sign, saying: "Not opened except by your hand."

sentences.zh: 直言貶二十年乃還，署帛宛然。

translations.literal: Zhiyan was demoted twenty years then returned; the signed silk was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyan was demoted twenty years then returned. The signed silk was as before.

sentences.zh: 及湯沐，發墮無餘。

translations.literal: At bath the hair fell without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that at bath the hair fell without remainder.

sentences.zh: 李孝女者，名妙法，瀛州博野人。

translations.literal: The Filial Daughter Li, named Miaofa, of Boye in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that the Filial Daughter Li, named Miaofa, of Boye in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山亂，被劫徙它州。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled she was seized and moved to another province.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled she was captured and moved to another province.

sentences.zh: 聞父亡，欲間道奔喪，一子不忍去，割一乳留以行。

translations.literal: Hearing her father had died she wished by hidden path to hurry to mourning; one child she could not leave — she cut one breast and left it to go.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing her father had died she wished by hidden path to hurry to mourning. One child she could not leave — she cut one breast and left it to go.

sentences.zh: 既至，父已葬，號踴請開父墓以視，宗族不許。

translations.literal: When she arrived her father was already buried; she wailed and leaped begging to open the father's tomb to see; the lineage would not permit.
translations.idiomatic: When she arrived her father was already buried. She wailed and leaped begging to open the father's tomb to see. The lineage would not permit.

sentences.zh: 復持刀刺心，乃為開。

translations.literal: Again she took a knife and stabbed her heart — then they opened it.
translations.idiomatic: Again she took a knife and stabbed her heart—then they opened it.

sentences.zh: 見棺，舌去塵，發治拭之。

translations.literal: Seeing the coffin she licked away dust and combed and wiped the hair.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that seeing the coffin she licked away dust and combed and wiped the hair.

sentences.zh: 結廬墓左，手植松柏，有異鳥至。

translations.literal: She built a hut left of the tomb, planted pine and cypress by hand; strange birds came.
translations.idiomatic: She built a hut left of the tomb, planted pine and cypress by hand. Strange birds came.

sentences.zh: 後，母病，或不食飲，女終日未嘗視匕箸，及亡，刺血書於母臂而葬，廬墓終身。

translations.literal: Later when her mother was ill she sometimes would not eat or drink; the daughter all day never looked at spoon and chopsticks; when the mother died she pricked blood and wrote on the mother's arm for burial, hut at the tomb for life.
translations.idiomatic: Later when her mother was ill she sometimes would not eat or drink. The daughter all day never looked at spoon and chopsticks. When the mother died she pricked blood and wrote on the mother's arm for burial, hut at the tomb for life.

sentences.zh: 李湍妻某氏。

translations.literal: A certain clan, wife of Li Tuan.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of a certain clan was wife to Li Tuan.

sentences.zh: 湍籍吳元濟軍，元和中，自拔歸鳥重胤，妻為賊縛而臠食之，將死，猶號湍曰：「善事鳥仆射！」

translations.literal: Tuan was enrolled in Wu Yuanji's army; in the Yuanhe era he escaped of himself to Niao Chongyin; the wife was bound by bandits and minced for food; about to die she still called to Tuan: "Serve well Vice Censor Niao!"
translations.idiomatic: Tuan was enrolled in Wu Yuanji's army. In the Yuanhe era he escaped of himself to Niao Chongyin. The wife was bound by bandits and minced for food. About to die she still called to Tuan: "Serve well Vice Censor Niao!"

sentences.zh: 觀者嘆泣。

translations.literal: Viewers sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Viewers sighed and wept," she said.

sentences.zh: 重胤請以其事屬史官，詔可。

translations.literal: Chongyin asked that the matter be sent to the historiographer; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin asked that the matter be sent to the historiographer. The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 董昌齡母楊，世居蔡。

translations.literal: Yang, mother of Dong Changling, clan long dwelt in Cai.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that yang, mother of Dong Changling, clan long dwelt in Cai.

sentences.zh: 昌齡更事吳少陽，至元濟時，為吳房令。

translations.literal: Changling changed service to Wu Shaoyang; by Yuanji's time he was magistrate of Wu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Changling changed service to Wu Shaoyang. By Yuanji's time he was magistrate of Wu Fang.

sentences.zh: 母常密戒曰：「逆順成敗，兒可圖之。」

translations.literal: The mother often secretly warned: "Rebellion and submission, success and failure — the son may plot."
translations.idiomatic: The mother often secretly warned: "Rebellion and submission, success and failure—the son may plot."

sentences.zh: 昌齡未決，徒郾城，楊復曰：「逆賊欺天，神所不福。

translations.literal: Changling had not decided; he was moved to Yancheng; Yang again said: "Rebel bandits deceive Heaven — spirits do not bless.
translations.idiomatic: Changling had not decided. He was moved to Yancheng. Yang again said: "Rebel bandits deceive Heaven — spirits do not bless.

sentences.zh: 當逆降，無以我累。

translations.literal: You should turn and submit; do not make me a burden.
translations.idiomatic: You should turn and submit. Do not make me a burden.

sentences.zh: 兒為忠臣，吾死不慊。」

translations.literal: The son as loyal minister — my death is not regret."
translations.idiomatic: So it was that the son as loyal minister — my death is not regret."

sentences.zh: 會王師逼郾城，昌齡乃降。

translations.literal: When the royal army pressed Yancheng, Changling then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal army pressed Yancheng, Changling then submitted," she said.

sentences.zh: 憲宗喜，即拜郾城令兼監察御史，昌齡謝曰：「母之訓也，臣何能！」

translations.literal: Xianzong rejoiced, immediately appointed Changling magistrate of Yancheng and concurrent investigating censor; Changling thanked saying: "Mother's instruction — how could your servant!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong rejoiced, immediately appointed Changling magistrate of Yancheng and concurrent investigating censor; Changling thanked saying: "Mother's instruction — how could your servant!"

sentences.zh: 帝嗟嘆。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration," she said.

sentences.zh: 元濟囚楊，欲殺者屢矣。

translations.literal: Yuanji imprisoned Yang; those who wished to kill her were many.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji imprisoned Yang. Those who wished to kill her were many.

sentences.zh: 蔡平而母在，陳許節度李遜表之，封北平郡太君。

translations.literal: When Cai was pacified the mother still lived; Chenxu military commissioner Li Xun memorialized her; enfeoffed Lady of Beiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai was pacified the mother still lived; Chenxu military commissioner Li Xun submitted a memorial her; enfeoffed Lady of Beiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 王孝女，徐州人，字和子。

translations.literal: Hezi the Filial Daughter Wang, of Xuzhou, courtesy name Hezi.
translations.idiomatic: Hezi the filial daughter Wang, of Xuzhou, courtesy name Hezi.

sentences.zh: 元和中，父兄皆防秋屯涇州，葉蕃寇邊，並戰死。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era father and elder brother all garrisoned autumn defense at Jingzhou; Ye Fan raided the border and all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era father and elder brother all garrisoned autumn defense at Jingzhou. Ye Fan raided the border and all died in battle.

sentences.zh: 和子年十七，單身被發徒跣蓑裳抵涇屯，日丐貸，護二喪還，葬於鄉，植松柏，翦發壞容，廬墓所。

translations.literal: Hezi at seventeen, alone, loosed hair, barefoot in rush cloak reached the Jing garrison, daily begged borrowed goods, escorted both coffins back, buried in the village, planted pine and cypress, cut hair and marred her face, hut at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that hezi at seventeen, alone, loosed hair, barefoot in rush cloak reached the Jing garrison, daily begged borrowed goods, escorted both coffins back, buried in the village, planted pine and cypress, cut hair and marred her face, hut at the grave.

sentences.zh: 節度使王智興白狀，詔旌其門。

translations.literal: Military commissioner Wang Zhixing reported the facts; an edict marked her gate.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioner Wang Zhixing reported the facts. An edict marked her gate.

sentences.zh: 段居貞妻謝，字小娥，洪州豫章人。

translations.literal: Xie, wife of Duan Juzhen, courtesy name Xiaoe, of Yuzhang in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that xie, wife of Duan Juzhen, courtesy name Xiaoe, of Yuzhang in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 居貞本歷陽俠少年，重氣決，娶歲餘，與謝父同賈江湖上，並為盜所殺。

translations.literal: Juzhen was originally a Liyang gallant youth, heavy on spirit and decision; married little more than a year, with Xie's father they traded on rivers and lakes — both were killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhen was originally a Liyang gallant youth, heavy on spirit and decision. Married little more than a year, with Xie's father they traded on rivers and lakes — both were killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 小娥赴江流，傷腦折足，人救以免。

translations.literal: Xiaoe threw herself into the current, injured head and broke foot — people saved her from death.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoe threw herself into the current, injured head and broke foot—people saved her from death.

sentences.zh: 轉側丐食至上元，夢父及夫告所殺主名，離析其文為十二言，持問內外姻，莫能曉。

translations.literal: Turning she begged food to Shangyuan; dreamed father and husband told the killers' names, splitting the text into twelve words; she held it asking affines inside and out — none could understand.
translations.idiomatic: Turning she begged food to Shangyuan. Dreamed father and husband told the killers' names, splitting the text into twelve words. She held it asking affines inside and out — none could understand.

sentences.zh: 隴西李公佐隱占得其意，曰：「殺若父者必申蘭，若天必申春，試以是求之。」

translations.literal: Longxi Li Gongzuo by hidden divination got the meaning, saying: "He who killed your father must be Shen Lan; your husband must be Shen Chun — try seeking by this."
translations.idiomatic: Longxi Li Gongzuo by hidden divination got the meaning, saying: "He who killed your father must be Shen Lan. Your husband must be Shen Chun — try seeking by this."

sentences.zh: 小娥泣謝。

translations.literal: Xiaoe wept and thanked.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoe wept and thanked," she said.

sentences.zh: 諸申，乃名盜亡命者也。

translations.literal: The various Shen were names of bandits and fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: The various Shen were the names of bandits and fugitives.

sentences.zh: 小娥詭服為男子，與傭保雜。

translations.literal: Xiaoe disguised herself as a man, mingled with hired laborers.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that xiaoe disguised herself as a man, mingled with hired laborers.

sentences.zh: 物色歲餘，得蘭於江州，春於獨樹浦。

translations.literal: After more than a year of searching she found Lan at Jiangzhou and Chun at Dushu ford.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that after more than a year of searching she found Lan at Jiangzhou and Chun at Dushu ford.

sentences.zh: 蘭與春，從兄弟也。

translations.literal: Lan and Chun were cousins.
translations.idiomatic: Lan and Chun were cousins of one another.

sentences.zh: 小娥托傭蘭家，日以謹信自效，蘭浸倚之，雖包苴無不委。

translations.literal: Xiaoe hired into Lan's house, daily with careful trust serving; Lan gradually relied on her — even wrapped goods he entrusted without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoe hired into Lan's house, daily with careful trust serving. Lan gradually relied on her — even wrapped goods he entrusted without exception.

sentences.zh: 小娥見所盜段、謝服用故在，益知所夢不疑。

translations.literal: Xiaoe saw stolen Duan and Xie clothing and goods still there — she knew the dream was not doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoe saw stolen Duan and Xie clothing and goods still there—she knew the dream was not doubtful.

sentences.zh: 出入二箕，伺其便。

translations.literal: Going in and out of the two lairs she watched for opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: So it was that going in and out of the two lairs she watched for opportunity.

sentences.zh: 它日蘭盡集群偷釃酒，蘭與春醉，臥廬。

translations.literal: One day Lan gathered all the thieves to pour libations; Lan and Chun drunk, lying in the hut.
translations.idiomatic: One day Lan gathered all the thieves to pour libations. Lan and Chun drunk, lying in the hut.

sentences.zh: 小娥閉戶，拔佩刀斬蘭首，因大呼捕賊。

translations.literal: Xiaoe shut the door, drew her sword and cut off Lan's head, then cried loudly to seize the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoe shut the door, drew her sword and cut off Lan's head, then cried out loudly to seize the bandit.
